clue.text: Fires fed by woman with hot tip

indicators.note: a thing fed by something takes it in, so the woman goes inside the fires word

parts.note: to fire pottery is to bake it, so fires gives bakes
she is the pronoun for a woman
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A woman, warmed by the fire, passes on a hot tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like advice to go with 'hot', but it is a gratuity, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a gratuity or small sum given as a gift in parts of Asia and the Middle East.

clue.text: An area dwindling south of America?

definitions.text: An area dwindling south of America?

parts.words: An area dwindling south of America?
parts.note: the great rainforest of South America, shrinking through deforestation; 'south of America' hints at South America rather than a place below the USA

explanation.surface: A puzzled note about some region shrinking just below the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of America' reads as a place below the USA, but means within South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon basin is the vast rainforest region of South America, steadily lost to clearing.

clue.text: One has to watch small part of log

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a log, such as a ship's log, is made up of individual entries

explanation.surface: Someone on duty has to keep an eye on a small section of a log.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard posted on watch is a person whose job is to watch over a place.

clue.text: Suppress swallowing cap of boletus up like some mushrooms

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
something swallowing another takes it inside, so a letter goes into the suppress word

parts.note: to elide is to omit or suppress, as a sound in speech

indicators.note: the cap of a word is its first letter, here of boletus

explanation.surface: A forager stops themselves eating a boletus cap, being like some mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ELBIDE (B placed in ELIDE) backwards. 'cap' is a mushroom word in this surface, yet it only picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Many mushrooms are safe to eat, so they can be described as fit for eating.

clue.text: Energy stored by sulphur explosive put in protective case

indicators.note: a thing stored by others is held between them, so the energy word sits inside

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
HE is short for high explosive
heat is a form of energy

explanation.surface: A chemist stores sulphur-based explosive carefully in a protective casing.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a blade back in its scabbard is to cover it with a protective case.

clue.text: Jumping up to a level with expenditure of energy?

definitions.text: Jumping up to a level with expenditure of energy?

indicators.note: jumping letters leap out of their order, so the words up to a level are rearranged
spending something uses it up, so the energy letter is spent from the jumbled pool

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An athlete leaps up to the height of a bar, spending a lot of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'up to a level' minus one E (energy spent) are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the event.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletics event in which a competitor uses a long flexible stick to clear a high bar.

clue.text: Song originally accompanied by religious series of actions?

definitions.text: Song originally accompanied by religious series of actions?

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word song

parts.note: PI is short for pious, so religious
a ritual is a fixed sequence of ceremonial actions

explanation.surface: A song that began as an accompaniment to religious ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: such songs grew out of religious worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious folk song of African-American origin, often sung during worship.

clue.text: Outlaw not quite accurate when holding agents up

indicators.note: the shortened phrase holds the agents inside it
not quite says the accurate phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: dead-on means exactly accurate

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the agents word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: reps are sales agents, short for representatives

explanation.surface: A gunslinger's aim falls short when he's holding up some agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of the phrase for accurate; 'up' reads the agents word from bottom to top before it is held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a reckless criminal of the Wild West, a bandit living outside the law.

clue.text: Rot's beginning in thick bit of wood crack up on the boards?

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the wood word

parts.note: a copse is a small dense wood

indicators.note: beginning picks the opening letter of the word rot

parts.note: its beginning is the first letter of rot

explanation.surface: Rot sets in where a thick piece of timber splits, up on the floorboards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the boards' means the stage: an actor who corpses breaks into helpless laughter during a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre slang: an actor who corpses gets the giggles and spoils a scene on stage.

clue.text: Bitter German's certainly not cut up

parts.note: ja is German for yes, certainly
un- is a prefix meaning not
diced food is cut up into cubes

explanation.surface: A resentful German insists he is certainly not hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaundiced view is a soured, resentful one, coloured by bitterness.

clue.text: Don't hold back rent twice!

parts.note: rent is used in two senses: to let is to rent out a property
a rip is a rent, a tear in fabric

explanation.surface: A tenant shouting about having to pay the rent twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to act or speak freely and with full force, without restraint.

clue.text: Coronation Street delayed when one's missed match

indicators.note: one is I, and missing it means that letter is dropped

parts.note: Corrie is the nickname of Coronation Street, a long-running British TV soap opera
something delayed is late

explanation.surface: A TV viewer finds the soap was delayed, so an episode was missed during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like the football that delayed the soap, but it is the verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To correlate two things is to show they correspond, so match or tally.

clue.text: Someone holding another's hat above the peak

indicators.note: above puts the hat first, as a hat sits on top

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
a tor is a rocky hill or peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone is holding another person's hat high above a mountain peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes and keeps a prisoner is their jailer or kidnapper.

clue.text: Vague horror on the increase around bankers' district

parts.note: a little horror is a naughty child, an imp

indicators.note: around says the increase word wraps the district

parts.note: a rise is an increase
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A vague dread grows as banking troubles spread around the City.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking exactness or precision, so unclear or indefinite.

clue.text: It may come from clashing forces, sir!

definitions.text: It may come from clashing forces, sir!

indicators.note: clashing forces are thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A soldier warns an officer about the danger when armies collide.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it too: gunfire from two sides comes when forces clash.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunfire from two or more directions at once, met when opposing armies engage.

clue.text: Absent smile might result from blowing it

parts.words: smile might result from blowing it
parts.note: read the answer's first word plus a way: blow up, or scramble, the first word and the letters make smile

explanation.surface: An absent-minded person blows out the candles, and a smile might follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing it' means scrambling the first word: rearrange MILES and you get SMILE, so MILES is a way to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone lost in thought is said to be far off, not mentally present.

clue.text: Sports are what kept princess awake

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school sports
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Sporting activities are what kept the princess from sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fairy tale The Princess and the Pea, a single pea under many mattresses kept a real princess awake.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy-tale allusion: the tiny vegetable beneath the mattresses that stopped the princess sleeping.

clue.text: Narrowly defeat seed

definitions.meaning: to beat them by a tiny margin, as at the post
a small seed of fruit such as an apple

explanation.surface: A sporting report of a narrow win over a seeded player.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: beating a rival by a whisker, and the small seed in a fruit.

clue.text: Unit needed for electric guitar?

definitions.meaning: the ampere is the unit of electric current, commonly shortened
an amplifier, also shortened, is needed to make an electric guitar audible

explanation.surface: A musician asks what equipment an electric guitar needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the short name for the ampere, and for an amplifier used by guitarists.

clue.text: Small vehicle circling craft in the drink

indicators.note: circling means the vehicle word goes round the craft word

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car
art is craft or skill

explanation.surface: A small car circling a boat that has ended up in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, which suits the boat, but here it is a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic cocktail of gin and vermouth, so an example of a drink.

clue.text: River blockage keeps slowing down westbound duck

indicators.note: in an across clue, westbound says the assembly is read right to left
keeps means the blockage holds the slowing word inside it

parts.note: a dam blocks a river
rall., short for rallentando, is the musical direction for slowing down

explanation.surface: A dam on the river is slowing down a duck heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westbound' turns DRALLAM (RALL placed in DAM) backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the commonest wild duck, the male with a glossy green head.

clue.text: Burst into song?

definitions.meaning: to burst a balloon is to make it go bang
a popular song, a chart hit

explanation.surface: Someone suddenly bursting into song.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a sudden explosive bang, and a popular-music track.

clue.text: Late bloomer's core vegetation yields resistance

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter, here of bloomer
a thing that yields gives something up, so the vegetation word loses a letter

parts.note: verdure is lush green vegetation
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A late-flowering plant's green growth finally stops resisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yields' means the vegetation word gives up its resistance letter, R being the physics symbol; 'core' takes the central letter of the seven-letter 'bloomer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: not arrived or done by the expected time, so behind schedule.

clue.text: Kundera's hero in parts behaving less 29

indicators.note: the letters sit in parts of two words, across the join

explanation.surface: A literary critic comments on Milan Kundera's protagonist acting less prudently in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 is ADVISEDLY, so 'behaving less advisedly' means acting more impetuously.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning reckless, so behaving with less care or sense.

clue.text: Ship's company's reported for voyage

indicators.note: reported means the word is as heard, not as written

parts.note: a ship's company is its crew, here plural

explanation.surface: A shipping firm's name is mentioned in news about a sea trip.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship's company is its crew, not a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pleasure trip by sea, calling at a number of places.

clue.text: Definitely not from resident in close

indicators.note: a resident in a place lives inside it, so this word goes inside the close word

parts.note: near means close
of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'

explanation.surface: A firm refusal from someone who lives in a cathedral close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like a cathedral close, a walled precinct where people live, but it means near.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom: an emphatic refusal, meaning certainly not or no chance.

clue.text: Decorative chain lifted from hostel knapsack

indicators.note: lifted says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A decorative chain was stolen from a backpacker's knapsack at a hostel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' means stolen in the surface, but in a down clue it turns TELKNA, from hosTEL KNApsack, upwards. 'from' signals the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental band or chain worn round the lower leg, just above the foot.

clue.text: Not normally rue day, nor every day?

indicators.note: not normally means arranged out of their usual order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't usually regret the day, nor any day.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout the whole year, so applying to every day, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Have potential for cloaking rolling fat? It does

definitions.text: Have potential for cloaking rolling fat? It does

indicators.note: a thing for cloaking covers another, so the potential word goes round

parts.note: can means be able, have the potential

indicators.note: rolling means the letters of fat are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A garment that can hide rolls of fat? It certainly does.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a loose robe hides a figure's rolls of fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose tunic or robe, roomy enough to hide a fuller figure.

clue.text: Days lived surprisingly sensibly

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters turn up in an unexpected order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An observation that someone's days were spent with surprising good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: deliberately and after careful thought, so in a prudent, considered way.

clue.text: Mark seen in bacon and right through other meat

indicators.note: right through means the letter runs inside the meat word

parts.note: steak is meat other than bacon

explanation.surface: A butcher points to the marbling in bacon, which runs right through other meats too.
explanation.walkthrough: Streaky bacon is bacon with lines of fat running through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A line or stripe of fat, like those that run through streaky bacon.

clue.text: Get to the bottom of babble about troubled teen

indicators.note: about says the babble word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly at length, babble

indicators.note: troubled means the letters of teen are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A parent tries to understand the chatter of a troubled teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges the letters of 'teen', and 'about' wraps the babble word around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to understand fully, to see into a mystery or person's mind.
